title: FREE. FOR NOW.
narration: Alex wants to watch one documentary. Seven days free? Perfect. A few taps, a payment card, and he's in. He tells himself he'll cancel before the trial ends. Future Alex has this under control.

title: WAIT. I STILL HAVE THIS?
narration: Cut to breakfast, a month later. His phone lights up. Nineteen dollars and ninety-nine cents. Alex stares at the charge, then at his coffee. Apparently, future Alex was busy.

title: WHERE IS CANCEL?
narration: No problem. Open the app. Find settings. Find the account. Find something called membership benefits. He came here to cancel a subscription. Somehow, he's now reading about exclusive features.

title: WELCOME TO THE EXIT.
narration: Joining felt like walking through an open door. Leaving feels like navigating a building where someone keeps moving the exit signs. Why can a free trial be so much easier to start than to stop?

title: THE SECOND DECISION
narration: A trial and a subscription can be the same arrangement at different prices. The initial period costs nothing. Then recurring billing starts under the terms you accepted, unless you cancel in time. The important decision comes after the exciting one.

title: A JOB FOR FUTURE YOU
narration: On signup day, the benefit is immediate. The cancellation task belongs to next week. Then next week arrives with work, groceries, and a password you can't remember. Forgetting isn't proof you wanted another month. But the billing system may keep running anyway.

title: CONVENIENCE HAS TWO SIDES
narration: Automatic renewal can be useful. You probably don't want your music to stop halfway through a road trip because you forgot to renew it. The problem is when continuing becomes effortless while stopping becomes confusing, or when important terms are hard to notice.

title: NOT EVERY STEP IS A TRICK
narration: A password check can protect your account. A clear confirmation can prevent mistakes. Not every extra step is deceptive. What matters is whether the process helps you carry out your decision, or repeatedly steers you away from it.

title: THE SEARCH COST
narration: Back to Alex. First comes the search. A cancellation option can be buried beneath menus, labels, and help pages. Each screen is small. Together, they turn a simple intention into a task that needs time and attention.

title: BEFORE YOU GO...
narration: Then comes the offer. Half off your next month. That might be a good deal if you actually want the service. But Alex wanted to leave. Now he has another decision to make before he can finish the first one.

title: READ THE VERB
narration: Next, two buttons. One is big and bright. The other is quiet and gray. Continue might mean continue canceling, or continue your membership. Alex has to read the action, instead of trusting whichever button looks easiest to press.

title: THE BENEFITS PARADE
narration: Then the benefits parade begins. You'll lose access to this. You'll miss out on that. Those details can be useful. But a long parade can pull the conversation away from one basic question: do you want to pay for another billing period?

title: I WILL FINISH THIS LATER.
narration: Alex gets a work message. He closes the cancellation screen halfway through. He hasn't decided to stay. He also hasn't finished leaving. If renewal is the default, an unfinished cancellation can leave the subscription active.

title: THIS PATTERN HAS A NAME
narration: The Federal Trade Commission has documented cancellation obstacles and confusing interface choices in its work on dark patterns. These are designs that can undermine a person's intended choice. Our maze is fictional; it illustrates the pattern, not a claim about every subscription company.

title: A DIFFERENT BILLING DOOR
narration: Sometimes the problem is the wrong door. The app you use and the company billing you may be different. A subscription purchased through an app store can have its cancellation controls in that store's subscription settings. Check the receipt before chasing buttons.

title: DELETING IS NOT CANCELING
narration: Dragging an app into the trash can feel satisfying. It also may leave the subscription running. For subscriptions billed through Google Play, uninstalling the app does not cancel them. The icon is gone. The payment arrangement can still be there.

title: START WITH THE RECEIPT
narration: So Alex changes his approach. He opens the receipt, checks who is billing him, and follows that provider's official cancellation instructions. Less wandering. A clearer destination. If the subscription isn't listed, he checks whether he used another account.

title: BEFORE THE NEXT TRIAL
narration: Before his next trial, he checks the renewal price, billing frequency, deadline, and cancellation method. He puts a reminder ahead of the deadline, with enough room to handle a problem. The reminder includes a link and the account he used.

title: CHECK WHAT HAPPENS NEXT
narration: Canceling early might be an option. But check the terms first. Some trials end access when you cancel. Others keep access until an expiration date. Don't assume that canceling today always means keeping every remaining day for free.

title: FINISH THE LAST STEP
narration: This time, Alex follows the process all the way through. He looks for the actual cancellation confirmation, checks the effective date, and saves the email or screenshot. Reaching a page about cancellation isn't the same as completing it.

title: TWO SEPARATE QUESTIONS
narration: He also separates two questions: have future renewals stopped, and can the charge already made be refunded? Those are different requests. Refund eligibility depends on the service, the circumstances, and applicable rules. Canceling doesn't automatically settle both.

title: IF THE EXIT STILL FAILS
narration: If the provider keeps charging after a completed cancellation, Alex keeps his records and contacts support. For charges he believes are unauthorized or incorrect, he contacts his card issuer promptly about options. He can also report deceptive practices to the FTC.

title: A SERVICE YOU CHOOSE TO KEEP
narration: A useful subscription can absolutely earn its place. Alex keeps his music service because he uses it. He cancels the documentary app because the movie is over. The goal isn't to cancel everything. It's to make the bill reflect a decision he actually made.

title: FREE TO TRY. CLEAR TO LEAVE.
narration: The best time to find the exit is before you walk in. A free trial isn't only a chance to test the product. It's also a chance to ask: what happens next, and how do I leave? Future you deserves an answer.
